change: Added chest->Clavicular Head as secondary: the landmine's diagonal bar arc engages the upper chest (clavicular head of pectoralis major) as a meaningful secondary mover, confirmed by multiple sources. Reordered secondaries for clarity (chest first, then triceps, traps, obliques).

Added chest->Clavicular Head as secondary (same diagonal bar path rationale as other landmine press variants). Completed Quads entry by adding Vastus Medialis — all three quad heads are recruited during the leg drive dip-and-drive; the original had only Rectus Femoris + Vastus Lateralis.

Added chest->Clavicular Head as secondary: the landmine arc consistently activates the upper chest regardless of standing/staggered vs. seated stance. Confirmed by sources covering all landmine press standing variants.

Added chest->Clavicular Head as secondary: the press portion of the squat-and-press follows the same landmine diagonal arc that activates the upper chest. Sources specifically list pectorals/upper chest among muscles worked for this compound movement.

Demoted Abductor (TFL/hip abductor region) from primary to secondary: EMG research shows Gluteus Medius is the dominant prime mover; TFL/abductor assists but EMG studies specifically note that proper band placement minimizes TFL compensation. Gluteus Medius alone is primary. Added Vastus Medialis to Quads secondary entry — all three quad heads are engaged isometrically holding the half-squat position throughout the exercise. Separated glutes into two secondary entries (Gluteus Maximus separate from Abductor) to comply with merge-same-bucket rule — but since original had glutes->Gluteus Medius primary and glutes->Gluteus Maximus secondary, these are already in separate entries by design (different role, same bucket is fine as separate primary/secondary split).
